checks.invariant: Caddy is the only internet-facing ingress to the backend: the uvicorn port is not published beyond the compose network.
checks.result: docker-compose.yml:9-10 publishes "8000:8000" with no host IP, so it binds every host interface. The port has been published since 2218cb2 and was kept when Caddy was added in b99bce4. uvicorn serves plain HTTP on 0.0.0.0:8000 (backend/Dockerfile:25). Caddy already reaches backend:8000 over the compose default network (Caddyfile:2), so the proxy does not need the host publication. Source cannot show whether a firewall blocks 8000, so this is filed as a needs_validation candidate.

checks.invariant: X-Forwarded-For is accepted as client identity only from the trusted proxy (Caddy).
checks.result: client_ip trusts the last X-Forwarded-For element from any peer in 127/8, ::1, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16 or fc00::/7 (auth.py:239-240, 259-263). The result keys the login throttle (app.py:440, 449), session ip (app.py:454) and the view_camera audit ip (app.py:731). Through Caddy the last hop is the real client, since Caddy's documented default (v2.5+, image tag caddy:2) replaces client-supplied XFF. A client hitting :8000 directly is trusted only if Docker presents it from a private address, for example docker-proxy IPv6-to-IPv4 forwarding, rootless or Desktop port drivers, or a host on the same private LAN. That is a deployment fact, so this is a candidate.

checks.invariant: Session-issuing responses carry a Secure cookie and HSTS, and credentials travel only over TLS.
checks.result: Secure and HSTS both come from request.url.scheme=='https' or X-Forwarded-Proto=='https' sent by any peer (auth.py:201-209, app.py:157-158). Via Caddy, X-Forwarded-Proto is https, so both are set. A direct :8000 login without that header sends the form password in cleartext and gets a session cookie without Secure and without HSTS. Mitigation: browsers that already received HSTS (max-age=31536000) for intivision.online upgrade http://intivision.online:8000 to https, which fails. Access by IP literal is not covered. The UI only cites http://localhost:8000 as a dev path (index.html:712). This is part of the port-8000 candidate.

checks.invariant: No anonymous broker carrying control traffic is exposed to lower-trust networks.
checks.result: The mqtt service (profile live) publishes 1883:1883 on all interfaces with 'listener 1883' and 'allow_anonymous true' (docker-compose.yml:48, mosquitto.conf:1-2). The active config sends the actuator to broker.hivemq.com, topic guardian/demo7k3x9/siren (config.yaml:48-50), through build_actuator, which both main.py and the backend use. The local broker therefore carries no application traffic today, so this is a hardening note. Siren control on the configured broker is owned by h4-mqtt-alerts.

checks.invariant: PostgreSQL is reachable only from the host loopback and the backend workload.
checks.result: Holds. Postgres is published only on 127.0.0.1:5433 (bd_intivision/docker-compose.yml:12-13) and joins the external vigia-net. Only backend joins vigia-net (docker-compose.yml:22-24); caddy, detector and mqtt stay on default. The password is required from the environment (${DB_PASSWORD:?}). The app connects as POSTGRES_USER vigia, which the postgres image creates as superuser. That is a least-privilege hardening note; SQL is parameterized.

checks.invariant: No workload can gain host or control-plane capability.
checks.result: Holds. No service uses privileged, cap_add, devices, host network or pid, or a docker.sock mount. Bind mounts are ./config.yaml (ro), ./events, ./backend/data, ./Caddyfile (ro) and ./mosquitto.conf (ro), plus the named caddy_data volume. Both images run as root because neither Dockerfile sets USER; that is a hardening note.

checks.invariant: Obvious-things checklist: debug gating, unprotected diagnostic endpoints, CORS, cookies, open redirects, TLS, error leakage.
checks.result: Debug: FastAPI debug is unset, uvicorn has no --reload, and /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json are off unless ENABLE_DOCS=1 (app.py:44-46), which compose does not set. Endpoints: only /health is unauthenticated and it returns only status and db state (app.py:516-522). There is no /debug, /admin, /metrics, /env or /config route and no static mount. CORS: no CORSMiddleware or Access-Control headers; CORP is same-origin. Cookies: HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, with Secure tied to X-Forwarded-Proto (see the cookie check). Redirects go only to '/', '/login' or camera UUID paths, so none are open. TLS: Caddy handles 80/443 with automatic HTTPS and a www redirect, but 8000 is plaintext (candidate). Errors: generic 401/403/503 handlers (app.py:386-407) and a generic 500 on analysis failure; no tracebacks are returned.

checks.invariant: Obvious-things checklist: hardcoded secrets, security TODOs, seed credentials, checked-in key/env files, dynamic code execution, dependency pinning.
checks.result: No hardcoded credentials in the current tree. No security TODO, FIXME or HACK comments. schema_vigia.sql seeds only plans and signals; there are no users. Users are created through manage.py with getpass and the password policy. No .env, .pem, .key or credentials.json was ever added (git log --all --diff-filter=A). No eval, exec, subprocess, os.system or unsafe yaml.load; settings uses safe_load. Dependencies are unpinned: >= ranges, no lockfile or hashes, torch/torchvision unpinned, opencv-python-headless force-reinstalled unpinned, floating base tags, and YOLO weights fetched at build. That is a hardening note.

checks.invariant: No reachable commit or branch tip contains credential material for the production site.
checks.result: git log --all -S basic_auth finds only b99bce4 (added) and 7345cc9 (removed). git show b99bce4:Caddyfile has 'basic_auth { angel $2a$14$M… }' inside the intivision.online block: a 60-character bcrypt hash at cost 14. These commit trees contain it: b99bce4, cfca76c, 89b2072, 747a21c, 352d16a, b11bddb, 1229858 and 41b30dc. It is also at the tip of remote-tracking branch origin/chore/aplanar-bd_intivision (747a21c). cfca76c added 'Caddyfile' to .gitignore, which does not untrack an already-tracked file. 7345cc9 removed both the hash and that ignore entry at the tip only. At b99bce4, backend/app.py routes had no authentication, so basic_auth was the only gate, and port 8000 also bypassed it. This is filed as a candidate.

checks.invariant: No other secret (Telegram or MQTT credentials, DB URL with password, API keys, private keys, real IPs) exists in tracked files or history.
checks.result: I searched every added and removed line in git log --all -p. Patterns: password, secret, token, api key, bearer, BEGIN, DATABASE_URL, URIs with userinfo, Telegram bot-token shape, bcrypt prefixes, ghp_, sk-, AKIA and IPv4 literals. Only placeholders turned up: postgresql://vigia:CLAVE@vigia-db (db.py:16), rtsp://usuario:clave@ip, and Wokwi-GUEST with an empty WiFi password. config.yaml has always had null telegram and MQTT credentials. Compose uses ${DATABASE_URL:?}, ${DB_PASSWORD:?} and ${TELEGRAM_TOKEN:-} indirection. The only IP literals are RFC1918 and loopback ranges. The topic guardian/demo7k3x9/siren works only as an obscurity value (owned by h4).

checks.invariant: Secrets, uploads, evidence and dumps are excluded from version control and from images built with COPY . .
checks.result: .gitignore covers .env at any depth, events/, backend/data/, *.mp4, *.pt, *.dump and backups/ (lines 10-14). It lacks .env.*, *.pem and *.key; settings.py loads only .env. .dockerignore excludes **/.env, **/.env.*, .git/, events/, backend/data/, bd_intivision/ and wokwi/. It does not exclude *.dump, backups/, *.mp4 or Caddyfile, so local dumps or videos at the repo root would be baked into images. No repo path publishes images, so this is a hardening note.

checks.invariant: Session and edge tokens use a CSPRNG, are stored hashed, are compared without a usable timing channel, and crypto failures fail closed.
checks.result: Holds. Tokens come from secrets.token_urlsafe(32), which is 256-bit (auth.py:140, manage.py:96). Only their SHA-256 hex is stored (auth.py:128-129). Lookup is SQL equality on that hash (auth.py:158, 220); with 256-bit random tokens an unsalted fast hash is adequate, and comparing hashes leaks no usable prefix. bcrypt uses the default cost with a 72-byte bound, and verify fails closed (auth.py:49-61). The CSP nonce is token_urlsafe(16) (app.py:490). There is no custom encryption, HMAC or JWT. The encrypted columns in the schema are unused by code.

checks.invariant: Secrets do not reach client responses, process arguments, lower-trust logs or other workloads.
checks.result: DB errors return a generic 503 (app.py:386-392), and no response contains configuration values. DATABASE_URL goes only to backend. Telegram and MQTT credentials go to backend and detector as environment variables, not process arguments; caddy and mqtt get none. manage.py reads passwords through getpass or an environment-variable name, and prints the edge token once to the operator terminal. notifier.py:66-67 and 79-80 log the requests exception text. On connection errors that text includes the URL path /bot<token>/sendPhoto, so the token lands in container logs, which only operators read. That is a hardening note.

candidates.title: Backend port 8000 is published on all host interfaces, bypassing the Caddy TLS ingress that client_ip and cookie security rely on
candidates.description: docker-compose.yml publishes the uvicorn backend as "8000:8000" with no bind address, so it listens on every host interface in plain HTTP. Caddy (80/443) is meant to be the only ingress and reaches backend:8000 over the compose network, so it does not need this publication. The backend's trust decisions assume all traffic comes through Caddy. A client that connects to :8000 directly, compared with one that goes through Caddy: (1) gets no TLS, so the /login password, the session cookie, /ingest bearer tokens and /ws/live frames cross the network in cleartext; (2) gets a session cookie without Secure and no HSTS unless it sends X-Forwarded-Proto itself; (3) chooses its own client IP whenever uvicorn sees it from a private address. In that case client_ip returns the last X-Forwarded-For element the attacker sent. The attacker can rotate it to escape the 30-failure per-IP login throttle, or set it to a victim's IP to throttle that victim, who reaches the backend through Caddy with the same last-hop IP. The same spoofed value is written to sessions.ip and to the view_camera audit_log ip. Docker presents internet clients from a private gateway address (172.16.0.0/12) when docker-proxy handles the connection, for example IPv6 clients reaching an IPv4-only bridge, rootless Docker or Docker Desktop, or for any host on the server's private LAN. Caddy itself adds no auth, rate or size controls (Caddyfile:1-3), so no application authorization is bypassed. Fix: remove the backend 'ports' entry or bind it to 127.0.0.1:8000:8000, and trust X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto only from Caddy's address.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: docker-compose.yml publishes the backend port on all host interfaces even though Caddy reaches the backend internally. backend/auth.py assumes every private-network peer is the trusted Caddy proxy (client_ip accepts X-Forwarded-For from any RFC1918, loopback or ULA peer). cookie_is_secure and HSTS assume TLS terminates at Caddy.

trace.description: "8000:8000" publishes the backend on every host interface, next to Caddy's 80/443, so clients can reach uvicorn without Caddy.

uvicorn binds 0.0.0.0:8000 in plain HTTP. Its default forwarded-allow-ips is 127.0.0.1, so it does not rewrite the client for proxied traffic and request.client.host is whatever peer address Docker presents.
The trusted networks include 172.16.0.0/12, 10.0.0.0/8 and 192.168.0.0/16, which cover Docker bridge gateways and private LANs, not only Caddy's container address.
If the peer is private, the last X-Forwarded-For element is returned as the client IP (line 263). A direct client that Docker NATs to the gateway therefore controls this value.
The spoofable IP keys the per-IP login throttle (throttled at 440, register_failure at 449) and is stored as the session IP (454).

evidence.description: Caddy proxies to backend:8000 over the compose network and applies no other control, so the host publication of 8000 is not needed for the intended ingress.
The client_ip docstring says an Internet client writing X-Forwarded-For by hand cannot pose as another IP. That holds only if no internet client reaches uvicorn from a private address.
cookie_is_secure trusts the request scheme or X-Forwarded-Proto from any peer. A direct HTTP login without that header gets a session cookie without Secure.
HSTS is emitted only when cookie_is_secure is true, so direct-port responses never carry HSTS.
The audit_log ip for an admin viewing another user's private camera comes from client_ip, so a direct-port client that appears private can forge it.
Caddy publishes 80 and 443, the intended TLS ingress for intivision.online.
The UI cites http://localhost:8000 only as a development path; nothing in the repo directs production users or edge devices to :8000.

blockers: The host firewall or cloud security-group state for TCP 8000 (IPv4 and IPv6) on the intivision.online host is not in the repository, so source cannot show whether the published port is reachable from the internet.

The peer address uvicorn sees for published-port traffic depends on the Docker daemon setup: userland-proxy, iptables/ip6tables, IPv6 clients reaching an IPv4-only network, and rootless or Desktop port drivers. Only a private gateway address lets client_ip accept attacker-supplied X-Forwarded-For.
Whether any user or edge mini PC is configured to use http://<host>:8000 is a deployment fact. In-repo clients default to localhost or https://intivision.online.
No OS-enforced sandbox was available, so the compose stack could not be run to observe the peer address or the Set-Cookie flags.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated Docker host with external networking disabled, start the backend service against a throwaway local Postgres with a dummy DATABASE_URL. From a separate network namespace, send one POST /login with dummy credentials and 'X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7' to the published port, over IPv4 and, if the daemon has IPv6 enabled, over IPv6. Check whether the 'Acceso fallido desde …' log line records 203.0.113.7 (spoof accepted) or the real client address. After one dummy successful login over the direct port, confirm the Set-Cookie lacks Secure and the response lacks Strict-Transport-Security.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner, on the intivision.online host: run 'docker port guardian-backend' and 'ss -ltnp' to list the 8000 listeners, read /etc/docker/daemon.json (userland-proxy, ip6tables, rootless), and review firewall or security-group rules for 8000 on IPv4 and IPv6. From an owner-controlled external machine, send one GET /health to the server IP on :8000 and one failed login carrying 'X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7', then read the backend log to see which IP was recorded.

candidates.title: Caddy basic_auth bcrypt hash for user 'angel', once the only gate on the production site, remains in git history and on a remote branch tip
candidates.description: Commit b99bce4 (2026-11-01) added to the tracked Caddyfile, inside the intivision.online site block, 'basic_auth { angel $2a$14$M… }': a well-formed 60-character bcrypt hash at cost 14. At that commit backend/app.py had no application authentication: /, /events, /evidence/{name}, /analyze, /ws/live and /ingest had no session dependency. That made this credential the only gate on the production dashboard until login arrived in 41b30dc. Port 8000 was already published, so the gate could also be bypassed directly at the time. cfca76c added 'Caddyfile' to .gitignore, which has no effect on a tracked file. 7345cc9 ('Caddyfile sin contraseña ni hash', i.e. Caddyfile without password or hash) removed the block and the ignore entry at the tip only. The hash is still in eight commits reachable from main (b99bce4, cfca76c, 89b2072, 747a21c, 352d16a, b11bddb, 1229858, 41b30dc). It is also at the tip of remote-tracking branch origin/chore/aplanar-bd_intivision (747a21c), where GitHub's file view would show it if the branch still exists. Anyone who can read the repository (assumed public) gets an offline guessing oracle with no rate limit or lockout. Cost 14 slows guessing to roughly a few hundred guesses per second per high-end GPU (estimate, not measured): a dictionary-grade or reused password is recoverable, a long random one is not. Nothing in the commits shows the password was rotated. The cfca76c attempt to ignore the Caddyfile suggests a server-local copy was intended.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: A production basic_auth password hash was committed into the tracked Caddyfile. Removing it at the tip (7345cc9) did not rewrite history or delete the stale branch, and nothing in source shows the password was rotated.

trace.scope: intivision.online site block at commit b99bce4
trace.description: b99bce4 added basic_auth with user 'angel' and a $2a$14$M… bcrypt hash at lines 2-4 of that version of the file, guarding the whole production site.
cfca76c appended 'Caddyfile' to .gitignore. Ignore rules do not untrack a tracked file, so the hash stayed in every later commit until 7345cc9 removed both the hash and the ignore entry.
The block was deleted at the tip only. Reachable history and the origin/chore/aplanar-bd_intivision tip (747a21c) still serve the hash to any repository reader.

evidence.description: git show b99bce4:Caddyfile shows 'basic_auth { angel $2a$14$M… }' (60 characters, cost 14). git log --all -S basic_auth lists only b99bce4 (added) and 7345cc9 (removed).

git show b99bce4:backend/app.py shows routes /events, /evidence/{name}, /analyze, /ws/live, /ingest and / with no authentication dependency. Session login arrived only in 41b30dc, so basic_auth was then the only gate.
"8000:8000" has been published since 2218cb2, so from b99bce4 to 41b30dc the basic_auth gate could also be bypassed through the direct port (historical).
cfca76c added 'Caddyfile' to .gitignore without untracking it, and 7345cc9 removed that entry. The current .gitignore has no Caddyfile rule.

blockers: Whether the Caddyfile deployed on the intivision.online host (mounted into guardian-caddy) still has basic_auth with this hash is a deployment fact outside the repository.
Only the credential owner knows whether the plaintext password is weak enough for offline guessing at bcrypt cost 14, or reused for their application account, server SSH, GitHub or e-mail.

GitHub visibility of the repository and of branch chore/aplanar-bd_intivision was not checked, because GitHub access is out of scope. It is assumed public, and local remote-tracking refs may be stale.

validation_plan.deployment: Owner inspects /etc/caddy/Caddyfile inside guardian-caddy on the production host for a basic_auth entry whose hash starts with $2a$14$M. The credential owner confirms whether that password is used anywhere else. If either is true, rotate the password and keep the new hash out of git. Delete the stale chore/aplanar-bd_intivision branch and, if the hash is still in use, rewrite history. Treat the old password as exposed either way.

hardening: The mqtt service (profile live) publishes 1883 on all interfaces with 'listener 1883' and 'allow_anonymous true' and no ACL (docker-compose.yml, mosquitto.conf). The active config.yaml sends the actuator to broker.hivemq.com, so no app traffic uses it today. It is still an open relay, and if actuator.host were switched to 'mqtt', anyone reaching 1883 could publish ON, WARN or OFF. Bind it to 127.0.0.1 or drop 'ports', and add password_file plus an acl_file. The siren-control boundary itself is owned by h4-mqtt-alerts.

Both images run as root: neither Dockerfile nor backend/Dockerfile sets USER. No privileged or host capability path exists, but adding a non-root USER limits what a backend compromise can write on the host through the ./events and ./backend/data bind mounts.

The backend connects to Postgres as POSTGRES_USER vigia, which the postgres:16 image creates as superuser (bd_intivision/docker-compose.yml:10). All observed SQL is parameterized, but a future injection would run as superuser (COPY … PROGRAM). Create a least-privilege application role for DATABASE_URL.

cookie_is_secure and HSTS trust X-Forwarded-Proto from any peer (backend/auth.py:201-204), while client_ip restricts X-Forwarded-For to private peers. Today a client can only harden its own cookie, but the two trust rules should be the same: trust only the proxy.

The audit IP is recorded inconsistently. The /evidence/{name} admin-view audit uses request.client.host (backend/app.py:682), which behind Caddy is always the proxy's internal address. The /cameras/{id} audit uses client_ip (app.py:731). As a result, evidence-view audit rows never contain the real client IP.

notifier.py:66-67 and 79-80 log requests exceptions. On connection errors the message includes the URL path /bot<TELEGRAM_TOKEN>/sendPhoto, so the bot token reaches container logs, which only operators read. Log a sanitized message instead.

.dockerignore does not exclude *.dump, backups/, *.mp4 or Caddyfile, all of which .gitignore treats as local. 'COPY . .' in both Dockerfiles would bake root-level DB dumps or local footage into images. No repo path publishes images today.
.gitignore lacks .env.*, *.pem and *.key patterns. settings.py loads only .env, so current impact is limited.

Dependencies and images are unpinned: requirements.txt uses only >= lower bounds with no lockfile or hashes; torch/torchvision install unpinned from the PyTorch index; opencv-python-headless is force-reinstalled unpinned; base tags float (python:3.11-slim, caddy:2, eclipse-mosquitto:2, postgres:16); YOLO weights are downloaded at build without hash verification.
The backend's HSTS header (max-age=31536000) lacks includeSubDomains, and Caddy adds no HSTS of its own. This is minor because the www host only redirects.

uncovered.surface: Shared ./events volume written by the detector container (profile live)
uncovered.boundary: Detector-written files in the backend-served evidence namespace
uncovered.subsystem: main.py / notifier.py detector pipeline and backend /evidence
uncovered.reason: The detector writes events.jsonl and intruso_YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS.jpg into ./events, the same directory /evidence/{name} serves (EVIDENCE_DIR). These files have no media_files owner. 'events.jsonl' and the timestamp-predictable intruso_* names match IMAGE_NAME_RE, so an edge token holder could claim them via /ingest and their community admin could then fetch them. This cross-workload volume path is not an explicit starting path in the /evidence or /ingest units; the parent should dedupe it against those units.
